verifiable-quality-gates.why: the change adds a build-comparison discipline and a reference script to this skill; a 'no new failures' claim must be provably able to fail, which is exactly this skill's core rule applied to comparisons.
verifiable-quality-gates.what: added the 'Comparing a change against a base build' section (compare on fields proven present; count worsening inside gates red in both builds; a clean claim must cite command, exit, output hash), the reference script compare-gate-runs.mjs, its reference doc, and a discrimination test that goes red if the script is a no-op.
quotes: test must FAIL when the check is replaced by a no-op

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the change stands up the executable BDD harness this skill's check-bdd-executed gate needs, and adds the first runnable feature + step definitions, so the scenarios actually run rather than only parse.
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: added the dependency-free runner bdd-run.mjs (reuses the Gherkin parser, emits Cucumber JSON), the features/ tree (config, the evidence feature, step defs driving the real script, append-only log, generated datastore), the CI bdd job, and a discrimination test for the runner.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment.

architectural-decision-records.why: the runner build-vs-depend choice and the build-comparison discipline are architecturally significant decisions with real alternatives and honest limits, so they ship an ADR in the same change.
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR-0091 recording the dependency-free executable BDD harness (vs adding @cucumber/cucumber vs not running the scenarios), the features/ + CI wiring, and the build-comparison rigor, with considered options and named limits.
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

pattern-selector.why: the runner was a real design choice under forces (this repo is deliberately dependency-light and guards its dependency-advisory posture), so the decision names the structure chosen on purpose and where the real guarantee lives.
pattern-selector.what: chose a dependency-free step runner over the full @cucumber/cucumber, recorded the forces, the two alternatives, and the real guarantee (the discrimination tests plus the standard Cucumber JSON contract that keeps it swappable) in ADR-0091's considered options.
quotes: the structure that fits the forces this system will actually face, chosen on purpose

skeptical-audit.why: the whole change is about not asserting a 'clean' or 'done' claim without evidence; the comparison claim rule requires a re-runnable command, exit code, and output hash, and the ADR states named limits.
skeptical-audit.what: made the comparison script print an output hash on a clean verdict, wrote the claim rule that a '0 new failures' claim must cite command/exit/output hash or stay not-assessed, and named the honest limits of both the runner and the comparison in the skill doc and the ADR.
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: both new scripts are tested at the layer that owns the risk (integration tests that spawn the real script), matching the test type to the risk rather than testing an extracted helper.
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: added integration tests that run the real compare-gate-runs.mjs and bdd-run.mjs against fixtures, covering the happy path, each fail-closed path, and the discriminating cases (missing field errors, worsening is reported, a thrown/undefined step fails the run).
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug

judge-arch.why: a wide change (two skills, new machinery, CI, ruleset) must pass a fresh-context review against the four questions before it is done.
judge-arch.what: ran a fresh-context subagent review of the full diff against the four questions and the two skills' disciplines, resolved its findings, and recorded the review in docs/arch-reviews/log.jsonl.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: offline dev tooling over repo-local trusted files (feature files, step definitions committed as code, gate-run JSON); no untrusted input, auth, secret, network, or user-facing surface. The scripts make no outbound web calls (enforced by the arch gate).

arch-encode.why: no new nearest-scoped rule file; the audit finding (a false 'clean' verdict) is encoded as a verifiable-quality-gates section plus a reference script pinned by its own discrimination test, not as an arch-gate rule.

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no personal or regulated data, storage, retention, migration, or backup is touched.

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: no running system, service boundary, data model, or scaling surface; CI tooling plus skill docs.

release-deployment-safety.why: no deploy, migration, feature flag, or rollback of a running system; the ruleset edit adds a required CI check but changes nothing that runs in production.

sre-operational-readiness.why: no running service, SLO, alert, or golden signal.

universal-accessibility-wcag.why: no user-facing UI; no .tsx/.jsx/.html/.css surface in the change.

usability-ux-universal-design.why: no interactive user-facing surface; the skill docs follow house style but there is no UI or flow.
